summary: REPAIR V3-08: the navigation must-fix from the previous cycle is resolved — app/index.tsx is byte-identical to the pristine accepted tree (openHousehold keeps setCurrentHouseholdId(id) + router.push('/add'); '/(tabs)' would resolve to the Unmatched Route screen and is not used). The candidate delta (scripts/finalizer-e2e.sh + its wrapper test) is a coherent, safe set of wrapper robustness improvements: boot wait 420s->60s (the android-emulator-runner@v2 action already waits for sys.boot_completed=1 before running the script, verified in the action source), settle 30s->10s, install bounded by timeout(120) with 2 attempts, single-attempt adb health check. Trusted verification passed (exit 0: typecheck, 453 tests, privacy 71, cost 21, expo export, prebuild, assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL) and all independent checks reproduce it. However, a must-fix remains: the concrete emulator blocker is NOT repaired. Step 7 of finalizer run 35650859523 failed after 20m59s=1259s; the step has no hard timeout (workflow sets no timeout-minutes; the action runs the script via exec without a timeout wrapper; its only timeout is emulator-boot-timeout=600s for boot). The E2E envelope (launch ~120-150s + waitFor('Demarrer', 900s)) plus wrapper overhead (~210-235s, dominated by a slow APK install) sums to ~1259s, so the failure is the app never showing 'Demarrer' within the E2E script's fixed 900s window (cold start / demo sign-in / app crash / dump fragility / System UI overlay). Reducing wrapper overhead cannot change that outcome because the E2E script's internal waitFor deadlines are fixed and the step has no hard timeout. The diagnostics artifact (id 10663681034) returns 401 and the step logs 403 from this environment (verified), so the blocker was reconstructed from the public API, the workflow, the action source and the E2E script. Decision: repair — keep the coherent WIP (wrapper improvements are safe and reduce waste), and require the next cycle to repair the actual blocker (app cold start / demo sign-in / initial render within the E2E fixed windows, or mid-wait diagnostics to capture the failure point).

findings.problem: The concrete emulator blocker is not repaired. The candidate's wrapper-timing changes (boot wait 420s->60s, settle 30s->10s, install 3->2 attempts bounded by timeout(120), single-attempt adb health check) are safe improvements but do not address the actual failure: the E2E script's waitFor('Demarrer', 900000) timed out because the app never showed the 'Demarrer' sign-in button within 900s of launch (cold start / demo sign-in / app crash / dump fragility / System UI overlay). The step has no hard timeout (workflow sets no timeout-minutes; android-emulator-runner@v2 runs the script via exec without a timeout wrapper; its only timeout is emulator-boot-timeout=600s for boot), so reducing wrapper overhead cannot change the E2E outcome — the E2E script's internal waitFor deadlines are fixed regardless of when the script starts.
findings.evidence: Public API: run 35650859523 step 7 'Android API 35 install, launch and golden path' failed 20:36:13->20:57:12 UTC (20m59s=1259s) with all gates and the x86_64 release build passing; diagnostics artifact uploaded. Timing reconstruction: E2E envelope (launch ~120-150s + Demarrer 900s = ~1020-1050s) + wrapper overhead (~210-235s, dominated by a slow APK install) sums to ~1259s, matching the step duration — the failure is the Demarrer waitFor timeout, not boot/install. Action source (lib/main.js, lib/emulator-manager.js) confirms no script timeout and a boot wait that already polls sys.boot_completed before the script runs. Artifact download returns HTTP 401 and step logs HTTP 403 from this environment, so the blocker was reconstructed from the public API, workflow, action source and E2E script. The candidate delta contains no logcat/dumpsys/result.json analysis and no change to the app cold-start/sign-in path or to the E2E script's diagnostics.
findings.requiredFix: Keep the pristine navigation (router.push('/add') + setCurrentHouseholdId(id)) and keep the safe wrapper improvements, then repair the actual blocker: the app must reach the 'Demarrer' screen within the E2E script's fixed 900s window on the API 35 emulator. Investigate the app cold-start / demo sign-in / initial render path (Hermes init, splash screen, SQLite demo seeding, sign-in flow) and/or add mid-wait diagnostics to scripts/e2e-android.js (periodic logcat/dumpsys during the Demarrer wait, not only at timeout) so the next cycle can capture the exact failure point if it persists. Preserve V3-01..V3-07 invariants.
